clue.text: Kind of letter that's written to be financially obstructive

blocks.note: first meaning: an upper-case letter written separately and clearly, as on forms
second meaning, read as a verb phrase: to hold up funds

explanation.surface: A letter seemingly composed to stall someone's money.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is the noun phrase; the second splits it as a verb and its object, block meaning obstruct and capital meaning money.
explanation.definitionFit: Forms asking for printing in separate upper-case letters ask for this style, and obstructing funds is literally stopping the money.

clue.text: Bishop, for one, whose position is determined by rank and file

definitions.text: Bishop, for one, whose position is determined by rank and file

blocks.clueFragment: Bishop, for one, whose position is determined by rank and file
blocks.note: surface reading: a churchman whose standing depends on the ordinary members of the congregation
setter's reading: on a chessboard, rows are ranks and columns are files, so a square is named by both

explanation.surface: A cleric's status depends on the views of ordinary churchgoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank and file' usually means ordinary members; here it is the grid coordinates of a chessboard, where a bishop is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is one of the pieces in chess, and every piece sits on a square fixed by its row and column.

clue.text: Test in Oval with area separating sides

indicators.note: something separating two things stands between them, so it goes inside

blocks.note: the letter shaped like an oval
right and left, the two sides
standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A cricket Test match being played at the Oval, a famous London cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is the London cricket ground in the surface but just the letter O in the wordplay; sides are right and left.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken examination, such as one in a language course, is a test conducted by speech rather than writing.

clue.text: Frank, Charlie and I would

blocks.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written
I'd is the contraction of I would

explanation.surface: Two men, Frank and Charlie, and the speaker would all do something.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a name in a list of people; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank means speaking openly and honestly, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Distort shared lines for aggressive marketing

indicators.note: to distort is to twist out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
L is line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Twisting jointly held lines of copy to push a product hard.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a pushy, high-pressure sales technique, the opposite of a gentle approach.

clue.text: Advocating for Mahler's first for concert

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the composer's name

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
the composer's initial

explanation.surface: Someone campaigns for Mahler's First Symphony to be played at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: Mahler's First is a real symphony, but here first just takes his initial. The Proms are a famous London summer concert series.
explanation.definitionFit: A prom is short for promenade concert, a performance where some of the audience stands.

clue.text: Composer discernible in subtle harmonies

indicators.note: something discernible in a phrase can be made out inside it, sitting within the letters

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A composer's style can be detected in his delicate harmonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian composer of operettas such as The Merry Widow.

clue.text: A couple of animals shot for host, say

blocks.note: taken as written
two animals: a nag (old horse) and a ram (male sheep)

explanation.surface: Two animals shot to feed a host's guests.
explanation.walkthrough: A couple of animals means two of them, a NAG and a RAM. The definition is an example: the letters of shot rearranged give host.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearranging the letters of one word to make another, as shot becomes host, is exactly this kind of wordplay.

clue.text: GBS and RLS, for example

blocks.note: surface reading: two sets of initials, George Bernard Shaw and Robert Louis Stevenson, both writers
setter's reading: people known by their letters, that is by initials, and also literary figures

explanation.walkthrough: Shaw and Stevenson are writers, and both are commonly referred to by their three initials, so the phrase works both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes scholars and authors, and these two writers are also literally identified by alphabetic initials.

clue.text: Players, guided, moved two men defensively

blocks.note: the cast is the set of actors in a show
to guide is to lead

explanation.surface: Players were guided and shifted two men into a defensive position.
explanation.walkthrough: In chess, castling moves the king and a rook in one turn to shelter the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Castling is the one chess move that shifts two pieces at once, king and rook, to protect the king.

clue.text: Fellow holding me back is evil genius

indicators.note: back means the small word is read from right to left
the fellow holding something has it inside his arms

blocks.note: a don is a fellow of a university college
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man holding me back is a criminal mastermind.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university fellow, a standard crossword substitution.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil genius in the sense of a malign spirit is a fiend, the meaning of this supernatural word.

clue.text: Its players are a shade lighter than their traditional opponents

definitions.text: Its players are a shade lighter than their traditional opponents

blocks.clueFragment: Its players are a shade lighter than their traditional opponents
blocks.note: surface reading: a team whose players weigh slightly less than their usual rivals
setter's reading: the university's sporting colour is a paler blue than its rival's darker blue

explanation.walkthrough: Sportsmen at this university and Oxford win 'blues'; this university's is light blue and Oxford's is dark blue.
explanation.definitionFit: The English university competing against Oxford in the Boat Race wears light blue, a paler colour than its rival's.

clue.text: East European's craziness depicted in series

indicators.note: something depicted in a work appears inside it

blocks.note: a run is a series, as of wins
mania is wild madness

explanation.surface: A man from Eastern Europe has his madness shown in a TV series.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. This is an older spelling of Romanian.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Romania, in Eastern Europe, is called by this older spelling of the nationality.

clue.text: Neanderthal starting on all fours

indicators.note: starting points to the opening letter of each following word

blocks.note: initials of the three words

explanation.surface: A primitive early human who began by walking on hands and feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Neanderthal is used informally for a clumsy, boorish lout, which this short word also means.

clue.text: Going to be published before spring

blocks.note: a book that is out has been published
a bound is a leap or spring

explanation.surface: A book is set to be published before the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring looks like the season; it is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A train or ship that is departing outwards is going away from its base, the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Severely criticise Peter in theatre

blocks.note: first meaning: to slate a show in a review
second meaning: the surname of J M Barrie's stage hero who never grew up

explanation.surface: A critic savages a production of the play about the boy who never grew up.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics are said to slate a bad play this way, and the stage hero is Peter Pan.

clue.text: What seasonally encourages a romantic understanding?

definitions.text: What seasonally encourages a romantic understanding?

blocks.clueFragment: What seasonally encourages a romantic understanding?
blocks.note: surface reading: something at Christmas that leads to a loving agreement
setter's reading: under-standing, standing beneath the plant to be kissed

explanation.walkthrough: Understanding splits as under-standing: by Christmas custom, couples standing under this plant kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: The festive plant hung at Christmas invites a kiss for anyone who stands beneath it.

clue.text: Small and convenient mixed drink

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for small
handy means conveniently useful

explanation.surface: A small, easy drink combining two ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: Mixed belongs to the definition, not an anagram signal. A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, common in British pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer topped up with lemonade is a blended drink, so it is literally a mixed drink.

clue.text: A great American author or two

blocks.note: first meaning: Mark ___, writer of Huckleberry Finn
second meaning: an archaic word for two, as in 'never the ___ shall meet'

explanation.surface: Naming one or two great American writers.
explanation.definitionFit: Samuel Clemens wrote as Mark Twain, and the old poetic word for a pair is the same.

clue.text: A journey across river for legendary vessel

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for river
to go is to travel, a journey

explanation.surface: A trip across a river on a famous ship of myth.
explanation.walkthrough: Journey goes across, beyond, the river, so it follows it in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth, Jason and the Argonauts sailed in this ship to find the Golden Fleece.

clue.text: Look left on plane for its destination

definitions.note: a description: where a plane heads

blocks.note: an air is a look or appearance
port is the left side of a ship or aircraft

explanation.surface: Glancing out of the left side of a plane to see where it is heading.
explanation.walkthrough: Look is a noun, an air or manner; left is the nautical port side.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight ends at a terminal with runways, the destination any aircraft is heading for.

clue.text: Attempt to improve some wine circle

blocks.note: red is a kind of wine
the letter shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: Trying to make a wine society better.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something again is to make another attempt at it, typically to make it better.

clue.text: Slowly move young woman back, straggler

indicators.note: back means everything before it is read from right to left

blocks.note: to drag is to move slowly and heavily
gal is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Moving a girl back slowly, someone falls behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Back reverses the whole run of letters, not only the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lags behind the rest is a slow straggler, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Philanthropist's name inscribed in entrance

indicators.note: something inscribed in a surface is written inside it

blocks.note: a door is an entrance
standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A benefactor's name is carved over the doorway of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A philanthropist gives money to good causes, so is a giver of gifts.
